subject.title: [Feature]: Per-agent cost budget enforcement at the gateway level

question: Should OpenClaw implement native core per-agent spend-budget enforcement, expose a budget-capable plugin/admission API, or leave spend caps to external/provider-account controls?
rationale: The choice changes config/default surface, provider dispatch policy, persistent accounting state, and operator recovery/status UX, so automation cannot safely choose the product boundary.

options.title: Native core admission layer
options.body: Add opt-in per-agent budgets before dispatch with durable SQLite reservations/refunds, receipts, and status/doctor visibility.

options.title: Plugin/API-first boundary
options.body: Extend the admission/hook API enough for plugins or external systems to enforce spend budgets while core remains generic.

options.title: External controls only
options.body: Document provider-account, wallet, or proxy controls and close native enforcement as out of scope.

recommendation.title: Native core admission layer
recommendation.body: Add opt-in per-agent budgets before dispatch with durable SQLite reservations/refunds, receipts, and status/doctor visibility.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the closest existing usage-cost reporting and adjacent guardrail surfaces, and the remaining choice spans product, config, and runtime policy.
